title: Marketing Manager (B2B SaaS)
full_description_html:
Marketing Manager (B2B SaaS)

  • Location: Hyderabad (Onsite)
  • Experience: 3+ Years
  • Industry: B2B Marketing | SaaS | Technology

About The Smarketers

The Smarketers is a full-service B2B marketing agency that helps technology and industrial businesses accelerate growth through Inbound Marketing, Demand Generation, Account-Based Marketing (ABM), RevOps & MarTech, Website Development, and AI-powered marketing solutions.

We partner with startups, mid-market companies, and global enterprises across IT Services, SaaS, System Integrators, Cybersecurity, Manufacturing, Industrial Automation, Telecom, Healthcare & Life Sciences, helping them build a predictable pipeline, accelerate revenue, and drive measurable business outcomes.

At The Smarketers, we believe great marketing combines strategy, creativity, technology, and data. As AI reshapes the marketing landscape, we're continuously evolving how we work by combining strong marketing fundamentals with AI, automation, and modern marketing technologies to deliver better results for our clients.

About the Role

We're looking for a Marketing Manager with strong expertise in Inbound Marketing who can build and scale modern B2B demand generation programs while supporting strategic Account-Based Marketing (ABM) initiatives.

The ideal candidate understands how to attract, engage, nurture, and convert B2B buyers through content, AEO, GEO, marketing automation, lifecycle marketing, and data-driven campaign optimization. While Inbound Marketing and Demand Generation are the primary focus of this role, you'll also contribute to targeted ABM programs for strategic accounts.

This is a high-ownership role for someone who enjoys solving problems, working across multiple client accounts, collaborating with cross-functional teams, and delivering measurable business impact.

You'll thrive in this role if you're passionate about learning, comfortable working in a fast-paced agency environment, confident in leading client conversations, and excited about using AI and automation to improve quality, efficiency, and results.

Key Responsibilities

Inbound Marketing & Demand Generation (Primary)

  • Develop and execute inbound marketing strategies that attract, engage, nurture, and convert qualified B2B buyers.
  • Build and optimize demand generation campaigns across content, AEO, GEO, email marketing, landing pages, webinars, social media, and organic channels.
  • Create and execute lead nurturing programs, lifecycle marketing campaigns, and marketing automation workflows.
  • Develop content strategies including blogs, case studies, whitepapers, eBooks, landing pages, webinars, sales enablement assets, and thought leadership content.
  • Improve website conversion rates through content optimization, user journey improvements, and conversion rate optimization (CRO).
  • Partner with Sales and RevOps to improve lead quality, MQL-to-SQL conversion, pipeline generation, and revenue contribution.
  • Support SEO-driven content initiatives and improve visibility across modern search experiences, AI-assisted discovery, and relevant industry communities.

Account-Based Marketing 

  • Support the planning and execution of targeted ABM campaigns for strategic accounts.
  • Define Ideal Customer Profiles (ICP), account segmentation, account prioritization, and personalized engagement strategies.
  • Collaborate with Sales to align account-based campaigns with revenue goals.
  • Measure account engagement and optimize campaigns based on performance insights.

Marketing Automation & AI

  • Build and optimize lead nurturing, lead scoring, segmentation, lifecycle automation, and campaign workflows using HubSpot or similar platforms.
  • Leverage AI and automation to improve research, campaign planning, content creation, reporting, documentation, and operational efficiency.
  • Identify opportunities to automate repetitive tasks and build scalable marketing processes while maintaining quality and accuracy.

Analytics & Optimization

  • Track and optimize key metrics including website traffic, lead generation, MQLs, SQLs, conversion rates, pipeline influence, campaign performance, account engagement, and revenue contribution.
  • Build actionable dashboards and provide insights using HubSpot, Looker Studio, Airtable, DashThis, or similar reporting tools.
  • Continuously improve campaigns through experimentation, A/B testing, analytics, and business insights.

Client & Project Management

  • Manage multiple global B2B client accounts in a fast-paced agency environment.
  • Lead client discussions, present recommendations, and build trusted relationships with stakeholders.
  • Collaborate closely with Sales, RevOps, Content, AEO, GEO, Paid Media, Design, Development, and Leadership teams to deliver integrated marketing programs.
  • Drive projects with ownership, accountability, quality, and timely execution.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who combines strong marketing expertise with curiosity, technology, and ownership.

The ideal candidate will have:

  • 3+ years of experience in B2B Inbound Marketing and Demand Generation.
  • Proven expertise in content marketing, AEO, GEO, lead nurturing, lifecycle marketing, conversion optimization, and marketing automation.
  • Experience planning and executing multi-channel inbound marketing campaigns that generate measurable pipeline growth.
  • Experience supporting or executing Account-Based Marketing (ABM) campaigns is highly preferred.
  • Experience working with SaaS, Technology, IT Services, Cybersecurity, Healthcare, Manufacturing, Telecom, or other B2B industries.
  • Hands-on experience with HubSpot or similar CRM and marketing automation platforms.
  • Familiarity with LinkedIn Ads, Google Ads, email marketing, analytics, and performance marketing.
  • Strong understanding of the modern B2B buyer journey and revenue-focused marketing strategies.
  • Excellent analytical, communication, presentation, client management, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities in a dynamic agency environment.

AI & Automation Mindset

We're not looking for marketers who simply use AI tools—we're looking for marketers who know how to combine deep marketing expertise with AI to produce better outcomes.

You'll stand out if you:

  • Use AI to improve the speed, quality, and effectiveness of your work.
  • Build automations that reduce manual effort and improve consistency.
  • Apply critical thinking and marketing expertise to validate AI-generated outputs.
  • Continuously explore new AI tools, workflows, and marketing technologies.
  • Stay updated with evolving industry trends and best practices.
  • Proactively identify better ways of working and contribute to improving internal processes.

Why Join The Smarketers?

  • Work with leading global B2B technology companies across diverse industries.
  • Lead impactful Inbound Marketing and Demand Generation programs that directly influence business growth.
  • Contribute to strategic Account-Based Marketing initiatives for enterprise clients.
  • Be part of a collaborative, high-performance agency where ownership, innovation, and continuous learning are valued.
  • Work alongside specialists across strategy, RevOps, Content, SEO, Paid Media, Design, Development, and Marketing Technology.
  • Get the opportunity to experiment with AI, automation, and modern marketing technologies to shape the future of B2B marketing.
  • Accelerate your professional growth through challenging work, meaningful client exposure, and continuous upskilling.

Our Ideal Team Member

We value people who:

  • Think strategically and execute with excellence.
  • Take ownership and lead with accountability.
  • Communicate confidently with clients and internal teams.
  • Have a strong Inbound Marketing mindset with a passion for generating measurable business outcomes.
  • Understand how ABM complements inbound strategies to accelerate enterprise growth.
  • Embrace AI and automation without compromising marketing fundamentals.
  • Continuously learn, share knowledge, and adapt to change.
  • Thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced agency environment.
  • Are passionate about creating win-win outcomes for clients, teammates, and The Smarketers.

Craft Stories That Stay With People.

At HiQ Weddings, we believe wedding films are more than a collection of beautiful shots. They are stories shaped by emotions, details, music, and meaningful moments.

We’re looking for a talented, detail-oriented Cinematographer & Video Editor who understands the art of visual storytelling and has a passion for creating elegant, cinematic wedding films.

  • Organise footage, project files, and media assets systematically.

Experience & Technical Requirements

  • 3–5 years of professional experience in cinematography and video editing.
  • At least 2 years of hands-on experience in wedding film editing is mandatory.
  • A strong portfolio demonstrating wedding highlights, cinematic films, or related storytelling projects.
  • Proficiency in Adobe Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro, or equivalent professional editing software.
  • Familiarity with DaVinci Resolve, colour grading, sound design, and motion graphics is an advantage.
  • Understanding of frame rates, codecs, media management, and export specifications.
  • Experience with DSLR or mirrorless cameras, gimbals, and on-location production is preferred.

What We Value

  • A strong visual aesthetic and an eye for detail.
  • The ability to tell a story through expressions, emotions, and carefully selected frames.

  • A refined understanding of colour, composition, and visual consistency.
  • The ability to work independently, solve creative challenges, and meet deadlines.
  • Openness to feedback and the ability to translate creative direction into finished work.
  • Professionalism, accountability, and a genuine passion for filmmaking.

Job Details

  • Position: Full-time
  • Location: Chennai
  • Work Mode: In-person
  • Experience: 3–5 years overall; minimum 2 years in wedding film editing

We look forward to meeting creative professionals who care deeply about the art of wedding filmmaking.

title: AI Platform Engineer
full_description_html:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We are hiring a AI Platform Engineer to build the execution layer for Supabase's internal AI systems.

Supabase is building an AI-native internal operating system: a common way of working across the company where AI carries a meaningful share of the operational load rather than sitting alongside it as an assistant. We are standing up a new central team to build those systems, enable the teams, and embed AI operations throughout the organization. You are the engineer on that team.

The execution layer is yours. You will build the platform that actually runs agents: an event-triggered queue, a headless model-agnostic runtime, durable state so work survives a restart, a human review gate, atomic rollback, and full logging of every prompt, tool call and decision so any run can be reconstructed. You will build the evaluation layer that makes any of it trustworthy, because an agent that cannot be measured cannot be trusted with anything beyond reading. And you will build the agents themselves, across everything from executive reporting down to a layer of agents that watch the platform and improve it.

This is a governance-heavy environment by design, and that is the interesting part of the problem. Agents are risk-tiered from read-only internal data through to external-facing output, with review depth, evaluation requirements and human approval scaling by tier. Some capabilities are permanently off limits: an agent may read and report, it may carry a human-authored update into a system of record once a human consents, and it may initiate contact within a strict budget, but it may never autonomously write a commitment (an owner, a due date, a status) into a shared work system. Your job is to make that structurally impossible rather than merely forbidden.

You will be the only engineer on this platform. You will close open architecture decisions yourself, own the infrastructure end to end, and instrument the system so it reports its own return.

What You'll Be Responsible For

In this role, you'll:

  • Ship the agent platform to production. An event-triggered queue, a headless model-agnostic runtime (choosing the runtime is an open decision you will close), durable state that survives a failed run, a human review gate, atomic rollback, and complete run logging in the warehouse.

  • Own the evaluation layer, and switch on the gate that depends on it. Golden suites with behavioral assertions rather than intuition, judge criteria with a written rubric, safety cases that must pass on every run, and a CI gate that blocks a regression from merging. This is the precondition for every agent that does anything beyond read internal data.

  • Build and register the agent portfolio. Reporting, drafting, linting, triage and question-answering agents across the executive, team-lead and individual-contributor layers, plus a meta layer that observes the platform and improves it.

  • Enforce governance in code. Risk tiers the pipeline actually enforces, least-privilege credentials per agent, tool-permission gates, a decision audit log, and autonomy classes where the dangerous class has no code path rather than a warning label. Nothing runs without a registered owner, tier, tool grant and human gate.

  • Design how the system contacts people. A hard interruption budget per person, message bundling instead of a stream of pings, and a structure that gives something useful before it asks for anything. Adoption depends on this more than on any other single design choice.

  • Own the platform tooling. The compiler and validator, inventory integrity, and the paths that distribute context and capabilities into the repositories and chat surfaces where work happens.

  • Compute the operating measures from production data. A pipeline from raw system activity through to a computed maturity grade per team, defensible enough that a team can dispute the result and be answered with the query rather than an opinion.

  • Instrument the platform's own return. A ledger that logs the work each agent absorbs and computes the monthly figure, so the value of the system is a measurement rather than a claim.

How You'll Think

Recursive Thinking

You build the generator, not the artifact. When you need thirty agents, you do not write thirty agents; you build the inventory, the compiler and the distribution path that makes the thirty-first cost an afternoon, then a meta layer whose job is to watch the platform, find its drift and file the fix.

The evaluation layer is the same move applied to trust. You are not checking whether one agent is correct today. You are building the machine that decides whether every future agent is allowed to ship, which means the suite has to be right in a way the agent does not, and the thing that grades has to be graded too.

Inversion Thinking

You start from the failure and work backward to the design. The rule is that an agent may never autonomously write a commitment into a shared work system. The weak implementation is an instruction in a prompt. The strong one is that the credential in the agent's tool grant physically cannot set an owner, a due date or a status, so no amount of clever input, prompt injection or model error produces the forbidden write. You reach for the second one first.

Same for evaluation. Before writing a suite you enumerate how the agent can be wrong: an update that invents progress that did not happen, one that quotes a private channel into a public digest, one that is accurate and reads as an accusation, one that credits the wrong person. Then the suite is that list, each case caught before the agent ships rather than after it embarrasses someone.

AI-Native Execution

You use agentic tools on real work, in files and repositories, with the same rigor you apply to anything else you ship. You have a setup of your own and can describe it mechanically: what triggers it, what it is allowed to touch, where the human approves, what it logs, and how you found out the one time it went wrong.

That experience is this job, generalized. You are building for async engineers across 40+ countries who will judge the platform by whether it saves them an hour or costs them one, so you are your own first user and your own harshest reviewer.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

Must Have

  • Have shipped production LLM agent systems that other people depended on. Not demos, not internal showcases. Systems with operational history, real users and at least one incident you can talk through. Prompt engineering on its own does not clear this bar.

  • Design evaluations, not spot checks. You build golden sets, write behavioral assertions, define judge rubrics, set pass thresholds and gate CI on the result. You can explain why "we reviewed a bunch of outputs and they looked good" is not evaluation.

  • Have done deep API work against the systems work actually lives in, and have authored MCP servers. You know the specific failure modes of those APIs, not just that they exist.

  • Own infrastructure end to end in Python on GCP, with a cloud warehouse and infrastructure as code. You provision, deploy, monitor and roll back your own systems, and you close architecture decisions rather than routing them onward.

  • Have taste about how software contacts humans. You treat every notification as spending a limited amount of trust.

Strong Signal

  • Public work in this space. An open-source agent framework, an MCP server, an evaluation harness, or writing on agent reliability that other practitioners cite.

  • LLM observability and cost instrumentation. Tracing agent runs, attributing spend per run, and building the queries that turn raw logs into a report someone acts on.

  • You have built an internal platform that non-engineers adopted voluntarily, and can describe what you changed after watching them use it.

What Success Looks Like

  • The platform is boring. Agents run on a schedule and on events, state survives restarts, failed runs roll back cleanly, and every run can be reconstructed from its log.

  • Nothing ships unevaluated. Every registered agent has a real suite with safety cases, the gate blocks regressions, and when someone challenges an output the answer is a test case rather than an argument.

  • The dangerous action is impossible, not discouraged. An audit of any agent's credentials shows it cannot perform the writes it is not allowed to perform, and the audit log makes every consequential decision traceable.

  • Teams pull the platform instead of being pushed. Agents get adopted because the reports are useful and the contact is rare and well-timed, and each team ends up with at least one workflow that runs automatically.

  • The platform reports its own value. The work absorbed is measured and published, so the case for expanding it is made with data rather than enthusiasm.

What We Offer

  • Fully Remote

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

  • ESOP

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

  • Tech Allowance

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

  • Health Benefits

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

  • Annual Off-Sites

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

  • Flexible Work

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

  • Professional Development

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

  • ~400 team members

  • 60+ countries

  • 20+ languages spoken

  • Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

  • 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

title: Postgres Engineer
full_description_html:
Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Senior Postgres Engineer to join our Postgres Team and help maintain and expand the stability and functionality of our hosted Postgres offering . You’ll work closely with customers, partners, product, engineering, support and success, helping us maintain a secure, stable, performant, and functional Postgres foundation.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.

This role also requires strong working overlap with Americas time zones due to production support and on-call responsibilities.

What you'll own:

  • Build and maintain PostgreSQL extensions in C and Rust, with a deep understanding of internals — parser, planner, WAL mechanics, and MVCC

  • Diagnose and resolve issues in managed PostgreSQL deployments, including custom extension failures, core dump analysis, and performance bottlenecks

  • Own idempotent deployment pipelines across thousands of running PostgreSQL instances, including testing and rollout strategies

  • Collaborate closely with customers, partners, product, engineering, support, and success teams to maintain a secure, stable, and performant Postgres foundation

  • Deep expertise in PostgreSQL internals - query planner, executor, and storage engine mechanics

  • Proven experience building PostgreSQL extensions in both C and Rust

  • Strong knowledge of PostgreSQL's permission model: RLS, roles, and grant systems

  • Experience troubleshooting production issues in managed PostgreSQL environments, including custom extension issues, performance bottlenecks, and resource contention

  • Comfortable building, testing, and owning idempotent deployments across thousands of running Postgres instances

full_description_html:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

 

About the Role

We're looking for a Postgres Deployment Engineer to join our team and elevate our PostgreSQL offerings.

You'll work hand-in-hand with the PostgreSQL team and play an instrumental role in technical decision-making and refining internal methodologies.

The focus of this role is around owning stability and deployment of our products. This role involves ongoing contribution and co-responsibility for builds/deployments via our public supabase/postgres GitHub repository. This repository bundles an array of features/products into docker images and AWS AMIs, giving users the ability to run Supabase on our cloud and locally. This role will function has developed as a bridge between product and infrastructure teams to improve the reliability of product deployments and upgrades.

In this role, your primary responsibilities will include:

  • Packaging software into our supabase/postgres repo to using either nix language with flakes, or debian packaging depending on our required target

  • Supporting the expansion of knowledge in Supabase toward our platform release system so that developers can self service more and more over time.

  • Expanding on our github actions, our team tooling, and our testing/release approaches

  • Timely PostgreSQL major, minor, and extension upgrades.

  • Engaging in proactive identification and resolution of production issues in customer deployments.

  • Contributing to the creation/maintaining of best practices, tools, and tests to ensure enhanced stability and decreased deployment risks over time.

What we need

This role demands the following pivotal qualities:

  1. PostgreSQL Expert: A profound understanding of PostgreSQL and its associated tools. Familiarity with extensions, performance optimization, and best practices is essential.

  2. Infrastructure: Proven expertise in infrastructure management, tooling, and optimization.

  3. Self-directed & Initiative: At Supabase, we value independence and proactive problem-solving. We anticipate you to be a dynamic self-starter, thriving in asynchronous collaboration across diverse teams. Your knack for spotting areas of improvement and commitment to realizing those enhancements will be key.

What you’ll do

  • Improve the utility and efficiency of our PostgreSQL offerings.

  • Work with relevant teams to understand the issues around postgres stability, and apply those insights to the build/test/deploy AMI and Docker releases.

  • Contribute to the enhancement of our public GitHub repositories, especially supabase/postgres.

  • Develop and expand tooling and solutions within the Supabase ecosystem.

  • Engage with customers routinely, ensuring our solutions resonate with their needs.

  • Address and resolve GitHub and Support issues.

Must haves

  • 3+ years experience with PostgreSQL and its ecosystem.

  • Knowledge of ansible, Nix package management system (including nix flakes), packer, docker, qemu/kvm, aws, and kubernetes deployments is essential. Need experience with linux and darwin/macos aarch64 targets, as we maintain ability to build for both architectures

  • Must have experience with conventional and nix-packaged builds of C/C++, Go, javascript, and Rust based projects

  • Exposure to public cloud platforms and deployment methodologies.

  • Eagerness to improve and expand our development tools/stack.

  • Comfortable with regular interactions with customers

  • Willingness to work on an “integrated” system and approach to packaging. For many reasons, we cannot apply nix packaging to every component in our stack, nor can we just adopt Nixos in production. We have successfully laid the foundation for integrating conventional and Nix-based systems, with carefully validated choices including using flakes, etc. So, you must be willing to work within and help optimize this paradigm toward our platform development.

About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the role

Auth, written in Go (server) and with client libraries for TypeScript, SSR and for other frameworks and technologies, is one of the most popular products in the Supabase stack. We are seeking someone to help us build new and maintain existing Auth features.

What you’ll be responsible for

  • Designing and implementing secure, scalable authentication features in Go and TypeScript.

  • Working across the stack: from server-side protocols to client-side libraries for frameworks like Next.js.

  • Owning the performance, reliability, and scalability of the Auth server across Supabase's infrastructure.

  • Contributing to the evolution of our Auth architecture, including support for OAuth, OIDC, SAML, and other protocols.

  • Planning and executing safe database migrations across a large fleet of Postgres instances.

  • Building and improving observability: metrics, tracing, alerting, and dashboards to keep the system healthy at scale.

  • Writing and reviewing RFCs as part of our product development process.

  • Collaborating with engineers across Supabase to ensure a seamless experience for developers using our tools.

  • Supporting the community and responding to developer feedback on GitHub, Discord, and other channels.

You might be a good fit if you

  • (Required) Have 4+ years of professional experience writing and shipping Go in production.

  • (Required) Have 2+ years of professional experience working on an authentication system (implementing protocol support, maintenance at scale).

  • (Required) Have strong relational database experience (Postgres or MySQL); Postgres experience is a bonus.

  • Have strong knowledge of TypeScript in addition to Go (languages used daily).

  • Have strong knowledge of web technology fundamentals (cookies, sessions, JWT, HTTP, browser APIs).

  • Have good knowledge of and deep interest in authentication security (passwords, protocols such as OAuth, OIDC or SAML, cryptography fundamentals such as hash functions, signatures and ciphers).

  • Have experience working with multiple web frameworks like Next.js (or other SSR alternative in the JavaScript space) and traditional web frameworks like Ruby on Rails, Django, Laravel or equivalent (in any language).

  • Have good technical writing skills (RFC process is an important part of making changes to the Auth product).

  • Have hands-on experience building and operating services at significant scale.

  • Have deep understanding of systems-level concerns: memory management, concurrency patterns, and compute resource optimization in Go.

  • Have experience with Kubernetes and AWS (or comparable cloud platform) in a production setting.

  • Have solid grasp of observability practices — metrics, distributed tracing, structured logging, and alerting (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry).

  • Have experience managing database schema migrations safely at scale.

What We Offer

  • Fully Remote

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

  • ESOP

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

  • Tech Allowance

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

  • Health Benefits

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

  • Annual Off-Sites

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

  • Flexible Work

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

  • Professional Development

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

  • 60+ countries

  • 20+ languages spoken

  • Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

We want developers to be able to build truly global applications by distributing both compute and data globally. Infrastructure concerns like regions, cold starts, CPU and memory provisioning should fade into the background so developers can focus on iterating on business logic, and fast, flexible runtimes a growing range of agent-driven code.

title: OrioleDB Developer
full_description_html:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the role

We're looking for an engineer to drive the evolution of OrioleDB and its collaboration with the upstream PostgreSQL community. OrioleDB is a next-generation storage engine for PostgreSQL, and this role sits at the intersection of database internals, open source community work, and Supabase's managed Postgres platform.

This role requires strong working overlap with Americas time zones due to production support and on-call responsibilities.

What you'll work on

  • New OrioleDB features. Design and implement new capabilities in OrioleDB — for example, native index access methods (GiST, GIN, HNSW for pgvector), disaster recovery tooling, and other storage-engine-level features that expand what OrioleDB can do.

  • Stability. Strengthen OrioleDB's reliability through deeper test coverage, fault injection, crash and recovery testing, and improvements to CI infrastructure. Ensure regressions are caught early and that OrioleDB behaves predictably under stress, replication, and failure scenarios.

  • Upstream collaboration. Contribute changes directly to PostgreSQL core. Part of OrioleDB lives as a patch on top of PostgreSQL — moving the right pieces upstream shrinks what we maintain ourselves and benefits the wider community. This happens through PostgreSQL's open development process: the pgsql-hackers mailing list, public code review, and commitfests.

  • Supabase integration. Work with Supabase's Postgres team to ensure OrioleDB fits naturally into Supabase's managed offering and roadmap.

You Will:

  • Design, implement, and test new OrioleDB features and integrate them cleanly with PostgreSQL's planner, executor, and surrounding subsystems.

  • Build out and maintain test infrastructure: regression suites, fuzzing, randomized testing, crash and recovery testing, and CI pipelines.

  • Identify and prepare patches suitable for upstreaming to PostgreSQL core.

  • Improve performance, resilience, monitoring, and operational tooling for production use.

  • Debug and resolve complex issues in low-level C code, including in storage, replication, indexing, and query execution paths.

  • Participate in design discussions, architecture reviews, and code reviews — both inside Supabase and in the PostgreSQL community.

  • Write clear technical documentation, design notes, and upstream proposals.

  • Contribute to troubleshooting, analyzing, supporting and maintaining OrioleDB in production deployments. This can include answering support ticket requests, an on-call rotation, and supporting our team members in troubleshooting and fixing live customer production databases.

You Are:

  • An existing PostgreSQL core contributor or have equivalent experience in Database internals.

  • An expert C programmer with 8+ years of production experience with focus on low-level systems programming

  • Deeply familiar with PostgreSQL’s codebase, build system, and extension APIs.

  • Have experience designing or implementing database storage engines, index structures, or query execution components.

  • Comfortable contributing to community‑driven, upstream open source projects.

  • Proficient in debugging and profiling complex C code in a database context.

  • Able to write clear technical documentation and explain design trade‑offs.

  • A strong communicator, committed to an open and collaborative development process.

title: Software Engineer - Storage
full_description_html:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

Supabase Storage is a scalable and high performance object storage service and is one of our fastest growing services. The current landscape of tools for uploading, storing, processing and delivering assets is complicated. Developers are forced to think about regions, caching, codecs and security before they can start uploading anything.

We are looking for engineers to solve this problem once and for all!

You will be working across the entire stack - client libraries, CLI, CDN, the storage server and the deployment infrastructure. One day, you might focus on improving upload resilience in iOS applications; the next, you could be optimizing the S3 protocol for efficient retries or finding ways to accelerate upload processing.

You will be contributing to both our open source server and upstream dependencies we use, like the TUS server.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.

title: Engineering Manager
full_description_html:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We're looking for Engineering Managers to lead engineering teams across Supabase. Teams range from developer-facing surfaces, core backend services, Platform, EngOps, and Databases.

This is a single pipeline for engineering management. As we get to know your background, we'll match you to the team where your experience and interests overlap most strongly. The Engineering Manager is a people, delivery, and technical role. Although we don’t expect managers to contribute to code directly, we do expect you to participate in design discussions and to be involved in setting the bar for engineering quality and best practices.

This is a new role at Supabase. We've historically optimised for technical excellence on every axis, including leadership. As our engineering org grows, people leadership has become just as critical, and the Engineering Manager role exists to reflect that. You'll be shaping what this role looks like from day one.

What You'll Be Responsible For

Team & People

  • Build a healthy, high-trust team culture in a remote-first, globally distributed environment.

  • Run 1:1s, performance management, career development, and onboarding for your direct reports.

  • Handle people admin (leave, time off, etc.) for your team.

Hiring

  • Own the hiring plan for your team and act as Hiring Manager. First round of interviewer for all roles on the team.

  • Partner with Talent Acquisition to source, interview, and close strong candidates.

  • Contribute to headcount planning, org design, and the evolution of engineering leadership at Supabase.

Delivery & Roadmap

  • Own the team's roadmap and project management (Linear), driving accountability and clear milestones.

  • Manage workflow intake and Slack triage. These are the team’s primary inboxes for cross-team requests. You decide what gets routed where, prioritized, or pushed back on.

  • Own the team's weekly updates and keep stakeholders aligned without creating overhead.

  • Organize effort against support tickets and maintain the team's SLO.

  • Surface risks, dependencies, and tradeoffs early and clearly to leadership.

Incident Commander

  • Train as an Incident Commander. Drive coordination, resolution, and post-incident follow-up.

  • Lead blameless post-incident reviews

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

  • Have 5+ years of engineering background, with enough depth to be credible with engineers building complex systems.

  • Have 3+ years managing remote engineering teams.

  • Have managed engineering teams at a cloud, SaaS, or developer tools company. Experience with developer tools or databases is a strong preference, but we'll consider any sufficiently technical background where you can demonstrate the ability to ramp on a new domain.

  • Have managed remote, globally distributed teams that work asynchronously across disparate time zones.

  • Are technical enough to be credible with strong engineers, but genuinely passionate about people management. This is the work you want to do, not a track you're settling for.

  • Build psychological safety and a feedback culture: you give feedback often and in the moment, ask for it back, and create space for the team to do the same.

  • Operate as a multiplier. Focused on helping individuals achieve more than they could alone, not on being the best technical voice in the room.

  • Coach rather than direct. Remove blockers, connect people to context and resources, and trust your engineers to own how the work gets done.

  • Have a real track record of performance management and can speak to specific examples of difficult conversations and how you navigated them.

  • Are comfortable with ambiguity and capable of building structure where there isn't much.

  • Communicate clearly and write well. You're default async, default written, set context proactively, and surface risks early.

title: Site Reliability Engineer
full_description_html:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

Supabase manages millions of Postgres instances and is growing. We have strong teams across observability, release engineering, and incident management — and we're concentrating our reliability efforts into a dedicated SRE practice that ties the discipline together across the platform.

You'll be embedded within Service Operations, and your primary job is to make every engineering team more reliable — not by owning their infrastructure, but by establishing the practices, frameworks, and feedback loops that let them own reliability themselves. You'll work across the org: sometimes setting the standard, sometimes pair-programming a fix, sometimes helping a team define their error budget, sometimes telling them it's exhausted.

This role is ideal for someone who has a strong vision for how SRE should work and thrives in async, fast-paced environments where influence matters more than authority.

What You'll Own

  • Partner with service teams to define meaningful SLIs and SLOs grounded in customer experience, and build the error budget policies that turn them into engineering decisions

  • Own and evolve the Operational Readiness Review (ORR) process — conducting reviews for new services and major changes across observability, alerting, runbooks, capacity, and graceful degradation

  • Strengthen the incident-to-improvement pipeline: connecting postmortem findings to operational readiness gaps, identifying repeat failure patterns, and driving systemic fixes

  • Act as the reliability expert teams pull in for architecture reviews, failure mode analysis, dependency mapping, and resilience design

  • Identify and quantify operational toil across the org, and build or advocate for automation that eliminates it

  • Help teams design sustainable on-call practices: alert quality, escalation paths, runbook coverage, and noise reduction

  • Track and report on org-wide operational maturity, surfacing systemic gaps and driving remediation

We're hiring experienced performance engineers to find and land performance wins across the Supabase stack — from the query optimiser to block device level, and across the network paths and cloud infrastructure that connect our distributed platform. This is a performance delivery role: real, measured improvements to our database, platform, and APIs as we scale toward enterprise and platform-grade workloads. About Supabase

About the Role

We are seeking a platform engineer to join our Compute Capacity team. This team owns the capacity plan that keeps compute supply ahead of demand across every region we operate in — the forecasting, buffer policy, and provisioning systems that make sure a project never runs into a wall it didn't know was there.

You'll work on the systems that turn a capacity plan into provisioned reality: reservation acquisition, fleet reconciliation, and the automation that keeps what we've committed to in sync with what we're actually running. You'll help build the metrics and alerting that let capacity problems surface months out, on vendor lead time, rather than at the moment someone needs the room.

You'll design, build, and operate systems that are both robust and highly automated — helping us hold the right buffer at the right cost, catch drift before it becomes a shortage, and give every team a single, trustworthy view of how much room we have across the millions of databases we manage.

About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the Billing team at Supabase. Billing owns the monetization and revenue systems that turn platform usage into accurate customer charges and finance-ready revenue data. The team’s scope includes plans, subscriptions, usage-based billing, invoices, payments, credits, coupons, taxation, dunning, collections, pricing mechanics, entitlements, marketplace and partner billing paths, and integrations with providers such as Stripe and Orb.

Billing sits at the intersection of engineering, product, finance, data, support, and partnerships. The systems are revenue-critical and trust-critical: they must remain correct, predictable, supportable, observable, and extensible as Supabase grows and introduces new products, pricing models, and partner channels.

This is a people, delivery, and technical leadership role. We don’t expect managers to contribute production code directly, but we do expect you to participate in architecture and design discussions, challenge plans with sound technical reasoning, and set a high bar for correctness, reliability, and operational maturity.

About Supabase

About the Role

We're looking for a FinOps Engineer to help drive cost optimization and cloud financial governance across our AWS infrastructure and GCP footprint. You'll work cross-functionally with Engineering, Finance, and Product to find and ship savings, build the tooling necessary to maximize efficiency of every dollar spent in the cloud, and cultivate a culture of cost awareness across engineering teams.

This is a hands-on engineering role, not an analyst seat. You'll do the schlep work other teams don't have time for, digging into a bucket's access pattern, writing the Terraform or Lambda that ships the fix, working on a product feature chasing a number until it reconciles, and influencing product decisions when cost to reliability tradeoffs hit. Strong communication matters as much as technical depth, you'll regularly explain a savings case to an engineering team, a finance stakeholder, and a leadership audience in the same week.

What You'll Be Responsible For

  • Find and ship savings across AWS and GCP: Analyze billing, usage, and cost trends to identify opportunities, rightsizing, storage lifecycle policies, data transfer, and spot/auto-scaling. Take ideas from identification through to a realized dollar figure, not just a recommendation.

  • Build and maintain cost attribution: Tagging policies, cost allocation, and chargeback/showback so engineering teams can see and own their own spend. This is foundational work other savings work depends on.

full_description_html:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We're looking for a SDK Engineer - Python to join our SDK team and own how developers talk to Supabase from Python. You'll work closely with the rest of the SDK team, our Auth, Realtime, Storage, PostgREST, Functions, CLI and Docs teams, and the open-source community, helping us make the Python SDK a library Python developers genuinely enjoy using.

Python developers reach Supabase from backend services, data pipelines, notebooks, and a growing number of AI agents and agent frameworks. The Python SDK is how all of them talk to the platform: database queries, auth, storage, realtime and edge functions, in both sync and async flavors.

This is a library-authoring role, and the work happens in the open: public repos, public issue trackers, and API decisions whose consequences last for years. If you get satisfaction from a type checker that catches the bug before your users do, from an async client that cleans up after itself, and from an issue tracker that isn't a graveyard, you'll like it here.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.

What You'll Be Responsible For

  • Build and evolve our Python SDK across database, auth, storage, realtime and functions, with both sync and async APIs that feel natural in Python.

  • Start new things. Alongside the maintenance work, find what's missing, make the case for it, and build it. Nobody will hand you the list.

  • Work in the open. Triage inbound issues, review and shepherd outside contributions, keep CI and release automation healthy, and hold a clear, kind line on scope.

  • Own the typing experience. Make the SDK fully typed and checker-friendly, so autocomplete and static analysis stay correct in real codebases.

  • Keep us honest across environments. Multiple Python versions, sync and async frameworks, workers, serverless and notebooks — with dependency ranges that don't fight our users' projects. Test it, don't assume it.

  • Work on realtime. Long-lived websocket connections, reconnection, and subscription and presence semantics.

  • Track the platform. When auth, realtime, storage, postgrest or edge functions ship a change, make sure the SDK reflects it, and that we say so in the changelog.

  • Design in public. Write the RFCs, migration guides, release notes and docs. Treat a breaking change as a deprecation path plus a migration story, not a version bump.

  • Make our SDK legible to AI coding agents, which are now a major consumer of it.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

  • Know modern Python typing deeply. You use generics, protocols, overloads and TypedDict as design tools, run strict type checking, and fix type errors without reaching for Any.

  • Know Python packaging for libraries: pyproject.toml, wheels, modern tooling, version support policy, and why libraries shouldn't pin their dependencies tightly.

title: Head of AI Native Operations
full_description_html:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role
We are looking for a Head of AI Native Operations to build the autonomous systems that run Supabase.

Supabase is building an AI-native internal operating system, where agents carry the operational load end to end. We are standing up a new central team to build that platform and run it in production. This is the role that leads it, and it is hands-on. You design the architecture, build the first versions of the critical pieces, and are accountable for whether every agent we run is correct, safe, and improving over time. We build rather than buy, and there are no settled best practices for most of this yet, so you will be setting them.

You will lead a team of senior individual contributors extending the platform and driving adoption across teams.

What You’ll Be Responsible For
In this role, you’ll:

  • Own the agent platform architecture: The harness and orchestration layer and connectors into company systems, shared context and memory, and the path from prototype to production.

  • Catch regressions before they ship: Model, prompt, and tool changes can’t ship until they pass the evals. When a new model comes out, you know within hours whether to adopt it.

  • Make every agent observable: Every run and every decision is traced. For any agent at any time, you can answer what it did, why, what it cost, and how its quality is trending.

  • Own safety and trust: Design the controls that let agents act without a human in the loop: least-privilege credentials, hard policy limits, escalation thresholds, audit logs, sandboxing, and prompt-injection defenses.

  • Replace workflows, don’t assist them: Pick the workflows agents can fully own today and take them to production.

  • Turn wins into a platform: Package what works into reusable components, templates, and eval harnesses so other teams can ship their own production agents without starting from scratch.

  • Build and direct the team: Hire and grow senior ICs, review their designs and pull requests, and hold the quality bar.

  • Measure what matters: Track workflows automated, eval pass rates, cost per run, and work absorbed against the hiring plan.



How You’ll Think

A Point of View on Where Automation Wins
You have a thesis about how AI and automation change the way a company operates, and it comes from building, not reading. You can look at a business and say which workflows agents can own today, which they will own in 12 months as models improve, and which still need people, and why. You defend that view with evidence from systems you have shipped, and you update it when the evals tell you to.

Eval-Driven
You don’t trust an agent because the demo looked good. You trust it because it passes a test set of real cases, and you know which cases it fails. When anything changes, your first question is “what do the evals say?”

Inversion Thinking
Left alone, an autonomous system tends to fail quietly, or people route around it. So the first question about any agent isn’t “does it work on the happy path?” but “how will this break, and how will we know?” The design follows from that answer: what the agent is never allowed to do, what it escalates, and which alert fires when quality drifts.

Recursive Thinking
Every system you build should produce the evidence that grades it. An agent isn’t done when it works. It’s done when it tells you, without you in the loop, that it has stopped working.

Must Have

  • Hands-on agent building: Have personally designed and built autonomous agent or LLM systems that ran in production and that others depended on. Prototypes, demos, and configuring a vendor tool don’t count. You don’t need to be a career software engineer, but you must have built these systems yourself.

  • Architecture depth: Can explain how the pieces fit together (orchestration, tool and data access, context and memory, tracing, evals, guardrails, deployment), with opinions on current frameworks.

  • Security judgment: Have shipped agents that take real actions with real permissions, and designed the controls that made that safe.

  • A tested point of view: Can argue, with examples from your own builds, where autonomous systems create real business leverage and where they don’t yet.

  • Technical leadership: Have led senior builders and set the quality bar through design and code review.

Strong Signal

  • Have replaced a human-run business workflow (finance, operations, support, release management) end to end with an autonomous system.

  • Are native to Git, Markdown, and pull requests, and comfortable reading and writing Python or TypeScript.

  • Have taken an internal platform from zero to adoption by teams you did not control.

  • A software engineering background is a plus, but not required.

What Success Looks Like

  • Six months: 20+ autonomous agents in production on the shared platform, each with an eval suite, tracing, and a named owner.

  • Regressions get caught, not discovered: Quality problems surface in an alert or dashboard before a user reports them.

  • Workflows replaced, not assisted: Multiple high-volume workflows are fully owned by agents, with humans handling only escalations.

  • Trusted by default: No agent causes material financial, security, or customer harm, and every agent’s permissions and actions can be audited.

  • Teams ship their own: At least three teams outside the core team run production agents built on the platform.

  • Autonomous team: Your two reports work independently, and you spend your time on architecture and review rather than execution.

full_description_html:
About the Role

We're looking for a FinOps Data Engineer to help drive cost optimization and cloud financial governance across our AWS infrastructure and GCP footprint. You'll work cross-functionally with Engineering, Finance, and Product to find and ship savings, build the tooling necessary to maximize efficiency of every dollar spent in the cloud, and cultivate a culture of cost awareness across engineering teams. This role owns the data side of that mission: the models, pipelines, and analysis that make cost, usage, and margin numbers trustworthy across the company.

This is a hands-on engineering role, not an analyst seat. You'll do the schlep work other teams don't have time for, digging into a bucket's access pattern, writing the dbt model or Python pipeline that ships the fix, building the cost-vs-revenue mart that answers a margin question once instead of every time, and chasing a number until it reconciles. Strong communication matters as much as technical depth, you'll regularly explain a savings case or a data model's implications to an engineering team, a finance stakeholder, and a leadership audience in the same week.

What You'll Be Responsible For

In this role, you'll:

  • Find and ship savings across AWS and GCP: Analyze billing, usage, and cost trends to identify opportunities, rightsizing, storage lifecycle policies, data transfer, and spot/auto-scaling. Take ideas from identification through to a realized dollar figure, not just a recommendation.

  • Build and maintain the FinOps data pipeline: Design and run the BigQuery/dbt models that turn raw billing and usage data (CUR, Storage Lens) into reconciled, trustworthy mart tables, the foundation everything else in FinOps is built on.

  • Build cost-vs-revenue and customer segmentation models: Model unit economics and margin by product line and customer segment, and extend coverage as new products and segments come online.

  • Apply data science to cost and usage data: Build forecasting models, detect anomalies statistically rather than by threshold alone, and quantify savings opportunities (e.g. storage lifecycle, request-cost patterns) with rigor a spreadsheet can't match.

  • Build and maintain cost attribution: Tagging policies, cost allocation, and chargeback/showback so engineering teams can see and own their own spend. This is foundational work other savings work depends on.

  • Automate cost governance: Build automated cost reporting, anomaly detection, and alerting. Write the scripts and infrastructure-as-code (Python, Terraform, Lambda) that enforce cost policy rather than relying on manual review.

  • Partner with engineering on architecture decisions: Bring cost into the room early, cost-efficiencies are cheaper to get right at design than to retrofit.

  • Work with Finance on forecasting and reporting: Support budget tracking and financial KPIs; build dashboards and self-serve analytics engineering and finance can both read.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

  • Have strong AWS expertise and working GCP knowledge, including pricing models, billing structures, and cost optimization mechanics.

  • Have data engineering depth: dbt, BigQuery (or an equivalent modern warehouse), SQL at scale, and data modeling for analytics (dimensional modeling, incremental models, testing).

  • Have data science fundamentals: statistical forecasting, anomaly detection, and experimentation, and know when a rigorous model beats a rule of thumb.

  • Have automation and scripting skills: Python, Terraform/ pulumi, Lambda, or Bash.

About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. More than 9 million developers and 250,000+ customers now build on Supabase, and the majority of new databases on the platform are created by AI app builders — so the systems underneath have to stay reliable while they grow fast.

About the Role

Container Engineering (ConEng) owns the internal container platform that runs Supabase's multi-tenant, multi-region services — the managed Kubernetes platform that other engineering teams build and deploy on top of. We own cluster lifecycle and cluster classes, multi-cluster and multi-region topology, capacity, scheduling, isolation and runtime safety, the higher-level platform APIs, the Kubernetes deployment contract and Argo semantics, rollout primitives, and runtime configuration and secret injection.

 

Your job is to make the platform itself trustworthy, observable, and cheap to operate at scale — and to raise the reliability bar for everyone who depends on it. This is not a gatekeeper role. You'll make the reliable path the easy path: building the automation and platform APIs that let product teams run safely by default, instrumenting what we operate, and making sure that when something breaks we detect it and recover fast.

 

The work spans three strength areas:

Tooling & ecosystem — deep knowledge of the container and orchestration landscape (Kubernetes, containerd/OCI, the CNCF ecosystem) and a clear point of view on how to compose it.

Software engineering — designing and building the platform's automation, controllers, and internal tooling as production code, including solutions that don't come pre-shaped by an existing tool.

Operational / SRE practice — the discipline (SLOs, error budgets, incident response, ORRs) that runs the platform at scale as a predictable one.

We expect you to be genuinely deep in at least one of these, and many of our strongest candidates are deep in two (usually leaning toward one). Bringing real strength across all three is rare and exceptional — and even then, no one is equally strong in all three at once, so you'd focus where you're most needed at any given time. Different profiles are welcome here; tell us which of these is your center of gravity.

What You'll Be Responsible For

Regardless of the skill set, all team members carry a share of the team's on-call rota, responding to platform incidents and driving them to resolution and follow-up.

Platform reliability & operations

  • Define SLIs/SLOs and error budgets for the container platform itself, and build error-budget policies that actually gate platform changes.

  • Own the Operational Readiness Review (ORR) process for new platform capabilities and major changes.

  • Design and track metrics for platform uptime, and increase observability into the platform by capturing the right metrics, logs, and traces across the platform layers.

  • Drive the incident-to-improvement pipeline: facilitate blameless postmortems, connect findings to readiness gaps, spot repeat failure patterns, and push through systemic fixes.

Software engineering

  • Build and maintain the platform's automation, controllers, operators, and internal tooling — writing production code and shipping it, not just wiring together existing tools.

  • Design and implement the platform-side CI/CD and rollout primitives that speed up platform deployments while working within proper change and release management.

  • Implement and maintain security automation for the platform: intrusion detection, automated remediation, and patch management.

  • Identify and quantify operational toil, and build the automation that removes it rather than just documenting it.

  • Contribute to the platform's continual testing automation — the test suites and pipelines that validate platform releases are fit for purpose before they reach tenants.

Tooling, ecosystem & architecture

  • Act as a platform reliability and architecture expert — contribute to failure-mode analysis, dependency mapping, and resilience design for multi-tenant container workloads.

  • Evaluate and evolve the platform's tooling ecosystem (orchestration, runtime, networking, isolation, and observability stack) with a clear, opinionated view on trade-offs.

  • Improve system architecture to reduce infrastructure cost while balancing security, reliability, and performance across tenants.

  • Guide teams building on the platform to design sustainable on-call practices for their own services: alert quality, escalation paths, runbook coverage, and noise reduction.

 

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

  • Have 5+ years in platform engineering, container/Kubernetes platform operations, SRE, or production infrastructure, and have operated production systems at scale and carried on-call for them.

  • Are genuinely deep in at least one — ideally two — of the three strength areas below (and tell us which is your center of gravity):

  • Tooling & ecosystem — know the container/orchestration landscape well: Kubernetes, containerd and the OCI/CRI standards, and the surrounding CNCF ecosystem (e.g. Argo CD/Argo Rollouts for GitOps and progressive delivery; Cilium/eBPF networking and the Gateway API; Karpenter/KEDA-style autoscaling; and workload-isolation runtimes such as gVisor or Kata Containers). You reason about trade-offs rather than reaching for defaults.

  • Software engineering — write real production code (Go and/or a comparable systems language) and can build controllers, operators, and platform APIs — stepping back to the underlying problem and building the right solution when no off-the-shelf tool fits.

  • Operational / SRE practice — are fluent in SLOs, error budgets, and operational KPIs; have led incident response and blameless postmortems; and have driven down MTTD/MTTR for systems you operated.

  • Have worked with large-scale multi-tenant systems and understand isolation as a spectrum — from namespaces, RBAC, network policies, and resource quotas through to stronger primitives such as virtual clusters (e.g. vCluster) or VM-class runtimes.

  • Operate confidently on AWS (multiple accounts, IAM, VPC) and are comfortable with infrastructure-as-code (Pulumi preferred; Terraform/CDK also fine) and Kubernetes.

  • Script and automate to eliminate toil rather than absorb it.

  • Communicate clearly with both infrastructure specialists and product engineers, and thrive in async, globally distributed teams.

  • Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and iterating toward better systems over time.

Nice to Have

title: Software Engineer - AI Tooling Infrastructure
full_description_html:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.


About the Role

We’re looking for a Software Engineer, AI Tooling Infrastructure to join our AI Tooling team and help build and run the backend services behind Supabase’s AI products. The Supabase MCP server is one example of what the team runs in production, alongside the services that support agent skills and the dashboard assistant. You’ll work closely with the Platform, SRE, Auth, Billing and Edge Functions teams, and with the engineers on the AI Tooling team who build the product surfaces.

The AI Tooling team runs its own services in production and carries its own on-call. Traffic from AI clients and agents behaves differently from traffic from people: hundreds of calls a minute, retry loops, and no reading of deprecation warnings. This role makes sure the services they use are reliable, correctly authorized and observable. It is a systems and infrastructure role rather than a product AI role, and it is not an SRE role. You will build and operate these systems, not only advise on them.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments, owns what they ship in production, and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.


What You’ll Be Responsible For

In this role, you’ll:

  • Build and operate the production backend services behind Supabase’s AI products, including the MCP server: deployment, scaling, configuration and release.

  • Take ownership of how those services are structured, including splitting or reshaping a service when that makes it safer to run and easier to change.

  • Define, measure and meet reliability targets for the services the team runs. Set SLOs with the SRE team, track error budgets, and use them to decide what to fix first.

  • Participate in the AI Tooling team on-call rotation, and be a first responder for incidents in those services. Investigate, fix, coordinate with other teams during incidents, and write the follow-ups and runbooks.

  • Work the AI Tooling team support queue alongside on-call, and turn recurring issues into fixes rather than repeated manual answers.

  • Own authentication and authorization for AI and agent clients: OAuth apps, scoped tokens, and permissions that make sense for agents as well as humans, including how we change or deprecate a permission without breaking existing integrations.

  • Own observability for the services the team runs: metrics, traces, logs, dashboards and alerts, so we find problems before customers do.

  • Handle capacity and abuse for agent traffic: rate limits, cost and safety controls, and behavior under load or when a dependency degrades.

  • Improve the architecture of the services the team owns as they grow, including splitting or reshaping a service when that makes it safer to run and easier to change.

  • Work with the Platform team on shared code, review ownership and release process, and with the SRE team on infrastructure, alerting and incident practice.

  • Contribute to the code of the AI Tooling team’s tools, such as the MCP server, where it affects reliability and security, in partnership with the engineers who own the product surface.


You Might Be a Good Fit If You

Must have:

  • Have 5+ years of experience building and running backend services in production, and have carried on-call for them.

  • Write strong TypeScript or Go, and are comfortable working in the other.

  • Have designed and operated APIs with real consumers: versioning, error handling, rate limiting, and backwards-compatible change.

  • Know OAuth, OIDC, JWT and API authorization well enough to debug them in production and to explain where implementations commonly deviate from the spec.

  • Have a good understanding of PostgreSQL and relational databases.

  • Are comfortable with CI/CD, Docker and containerized deployments, and with infrastructure as code. Any tool is fine.

  • Can debug across services: follow a slow or failing request through several systems using metrics, traces and logs.

  • Communicate clearly in writing, work with a wide range of stakeholders, and thrive in async, globally distributed teams.

  • Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and moving quickly.

Pick your centre of gravity. We expect you to be deep in at least one of these, and to tell us which:

  • APIs and auth: You have designed permission models, token scopes or OAuth flows for third-party or machine clients, and you have migrated them without breaking users.

  • Operations: You have run production services yourself: carried the pager, written alerts and runbooks, used SLOs or similar to decide what to fix, and made shared systems less risky over time.

  • Gateways and distributed systems: You have built or run proxies or gateways, or debugged hard failures across services (retries, partial failures, upstream outages, fail-open vs fail-closed decisions), and you can reason about load and degradation.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with agent tooling (MCP or similar), or serving traffic from AI agents and LLM clients.

  • Experience moving a service out of a larger codebase while keeping existing clients working.

  • Experience with Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Logflare or a similar observability stack, and real SLO work.

  • Open-source contributions, especially to Node.js, Go, TypeScript or API tooling.

What We Offer

  • Fully Remote

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

  • ESOP

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

  • Tech Allowance

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

  • Health Benefits

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

  • Annual Off-Sites

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

  • Flexible Work

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

  • Professional Development

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

  • ~400 team members

  • 60+ countries

  • 20+ languages spoken

  • Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

  • 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.
